doc.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001

chapter: Gloria Lynne, Milt Hinton and later work
title: Musicians' union and Playboy Club pension
summary: The union is dormant; May worked at the Playboy Club with Kai Winding and feels cheated on pension benefits.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: There’s a reason you’re doing that. That’s a good one. How’s the musician’s union been for you over the years?

It’s been kind of dormant really. But we have people in there like Bob Cranshaw and Jimmy Owens and people that are really and -- And at one time Benny Powell was in there really pushing them really to help, to bring jazz musicians up to par. So it looks, because I did a lot of things, I was in the Playboy Club for instance once for a while, playing with Kai Winding, then I had my own quartet there or a while. Because I just wanted to stay around town. It was a good place, to have a nice, steady jazz gig and you could go in and out. And they seemed to have put in all the benefits and stuff but they didn’t, so I feel kind of cheated for all that time I put in there. So Bob is trying to work on that for me. Because you know, it’s pension time now.
